pending.title: TLT Sell Signal Remains Intact | What It Means for Interest Rates
pending.description:
In this Wicked Stocks video analysis, we revisit the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) following the long-term sell signal triggered in late July.

TLT has declined more than 7% since the sell signal, while long-term interest rates have continued to rise. With the bearish structure still intact, we identify $74.41–$75.05 as the next major downside objective, potentially by the end of October.

A weekly settlement below $74.41 would reinforce the longer-term bearish outlook and open the way toward the low $70s over the following 3–5 weeks. On the upside, declining channel resistance remains the key level TLT would need to reclaim to indicate a meaningful shift in trend.

Because Treasury bond prices and yields generally move inversely, continued weakness in TLT would also indicate further upward pressure on long-term interest rates.

#Tesla gained more than 2% yesterday, closing at $378.73, extending its massive move from Friday.

So, the short-term buy signal is clearly playing out, but #TSLA is now approaching the resistance zone that could determine whether this remains just a rally within a larger bearish structure — or turns into something much bigger.

*

To remind you, the rebound began after #TSLA rejected the recent sell signal around $352.84. 

Reclaiming that important channel structure generated a 2–3 week upside objective at $396.77, and the stock has already covered more than half the distance in only a couple of sessions.

The first test is $384.59.

That channel top can contain intraday or even daily buying pressure. But a close above $384.59 would strengthen the breakout and could put $396.77 in play as soon as the following session.

*

On the downside, watch $367.95. 

This Fibonacci level is now important support and should contain selling pressure over the next several days. 

A close below it would suggest the rally has stalled and could send TSLA back toward $352.84 within 1–2 sessions.

*

But the real battle begins higher: $396.77–$401.08.

Despite the short-term bullish signal, this remains major sellable resistance. 

As long as TSLA stays below this zone, the larger six-month sell signal remains intact, with $229.41 still the long-term downside objective.

That makes the current rally somewhat counterintuitive: $396.77 is both the bullish short-term target AND the beginning of the major longer-term sell zone.

*

And $401.08 is the level that could change everything.

A weekly close above $401.08 would invalidate the longer-term bearish setup.

Instead of targeting the $220s, the technical outlook would flip toward the $540–$550 area over the following 3–5 months.

Conversely, if this rally fails and TSLA closes below $352.84, downside risk would accelerate again, targeting $331.50 within roughly a week and the $306 area over 3–5 weeks.

*

So, the updated roadmap looks like this:
– Above $384.59 → $396.77 likely next
– $396.77–$401.08 → major sell/resistance zone
– Weekly close above $401.08 → bearish thesis invalidated, $540–$550 becomes the 3–5 month target
– Below $367.95 → risk of a quick return to $352.84
– Below $352.84 → $331.50, then roughly $306

*

For now, momentum favors the bulls and $396.77 is coming into reach. But the much bigger question is what happens when TSLA gets there.

Can Tesla finally break through $401 and invalidate the long-term sell signal — or is this rally simply carrying the stock directly into its next major selling opportunity?

On the downside, $369.02 is the key support. TSLA could simply consolidate between $369.02 and $384.27 today or even through tomorrow.

And $352.84 is the much bigger bearish trigger.

Even though short-term momentum has turned bullish, $396.77–$401.08 remains major long-term resistance and a potential sell zone.

As long as #TSLA remains below it, the broader bearish structure remains intact, with $229.41 still the longer-term downside objective into Q1 2027.

*

But a weekly close above $401.08 would change the entire setup. That would shift the longer-term outlook decisively bullish and put the $540s–$550s in focus into Q1 2027.

– Above $384.27: $396.77–$401.08 comes into focus
